# Samuccayavāra (Pvr 1.16)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samuccayavāra* ("Summary of the previous six sections") is the sixteenth chapter of the first division of the *Parivāra*, the concluding book of the Theravāda *Vinayapiṭaka*. Functioning as a synthetic analytical summary, the text concatenates and integrates the classifications and determinations set forth in the preceding chapters. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates widespread canonical and paracanonical text reuse, identifying 500 matching passages across 31 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Parivāra*, it shares extensive phrasing with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4, comprising 125 matches), the *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), sister *Samuccayavāra* sections (Pvr 1.8, Pvr 2.8, Pvr 2.16), the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1, Pvr 1.9, Pvr 2.1), and the *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 1.2, Pvr 1.10) [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared with later Vinaya exegetical literature, including the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Vinayapiṭaka*, the *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā*, and the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language automated alignments link segments of the text to Sanskrit treatises such as the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* and Tibetan texts like the *Vinayasaṃgrahaṇī* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4040), though these reflect algorithmic similarity rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].

Direct citations or scholarly treatments of this specific text do not occur in the matched secondary passages, which merely register homonymous Sanskrit and Tibetan works incorporating the term *samuccaya*.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
